belief: I'll never get over losing them.
origins: Grief can feel endless, especially in the first year or after a sudden or traumatic loss. Well-meaning people may say “time heals” or “you should be over this,” and when it does not feel true, we conclude that something is wrong with us or that the pain is permanent.
teaches: Jesus said, “Blessed are those who mourn, for they will be comforted.” The psalmist says, “Weeping may stay the night, but joy comes in the morning,” and “The LORD is near to the brokenhearted.” Revelation promises, “He will wipe away every tear from their eyes.” Paul calls God “the God of all comfort, who comforts us in all our troubles.” Grief does not have a deadline, and many people never stop missing the one they lost. But the intensity softens, and joy and love can live alongside loss.
self_statements: I will always feel like this.
I cannot go on without them.
Life will never be good again.
Something is wrong with me for still hurting.
I will never be happy again.
errors: Predicting that the pain will never ease.
Believing I must either be over it or be in agony.
Insisting that I should be over it by now.
Feeling hopeless and concluding that things are hopeless.
questions: How has my grief changed since the first days, even slightly?
What do I need right now: rest, company, tears, or help with practical tasks?
What are healthy ways I can honor my loved one?
What does it mean to “get over” someone I loved?
How might God’s comfort come through people around me?
Who can I talk to about how heavy this is?
truth: I may always miss the one I lost, but the pain will not stay at this intensity forever. I can mourn, be comforted, and carry my love for them with me. God is near to the brokenhearted, and joy can return alongside the loss.
hw_truths: Weeping may stay the night, but joy comes in the morning.
God is near to the brokenhearted.
He will wipe away every tear.
Love and joy can coexist with loss.
log: Each day, write one comfort you received and one memory you treasure.
actions: Set aside time each day to remember and cry if you need to.
Do one thing in their memory, such as a visit, a gift, or a story.
Join a grief group or talk with a pastor or counselor.
Sleep, eat, and move gently each day. If you have thoughts of ending your life, call or text 988 right away.
prayer: Lord, I miss them so much. Comfort me as only You can. Be near to my broken heart, and carry me through the days when I cannot carry myself. Amen.
hw_questions: What do I need right now?
name_example: Sarah can write: “Weeping may stay the night, but joy comes in the morning.”
